# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about this carefully. I have the manual, but I can only communicate via gestures, and only Deaf can see my gestures. Blind cannot see anything, so I cannot reach Blind directly - only through Deaf, who can then... wait, Deaf cannot speak either (Deaf can only hear/see but the table says Deaf cannot hear or touch). Let me check: Deaf can see, cannot hear, cannot touch. Deaf's channels - can Deaf speak? The table doesn't say Deaf cannot speak. So Deaf can likely speak to Blind.

So the chain is: Mute (me) --gesture--> Deaf --speech--> Blind. I need to encode the manual's light-to-wire-color mapping into gestures Deaf can see and relay verbally to Blind.

Deaf needs to first see the bomb's actual light color, then combine with my manual info to tell Blind which wire to cut. I should wait until Deaf reports what light they see, but Deaf goes last in turn order (Mute, Blind, Deaf), so Deaf hasn't spoken yet. I should preemptively send the manual mapping via gestures now, since gestures don't require prior info.

Let me assign gesture codes for colors: red, yellow, green, blue.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "🖐"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👍"])
```

Wait, I need this to actually carry meaning - I should establish a code and explain it, but I can't speak. Gestures alone with no prior shared meaning are just symbols. I need to define a mapping using gesture sequences that Deaf can interpret combined with what they see (colors on bomb). Since Deaf sees actual colors/markings, Deaf can match my gesture-encoded manual to their own observation if I use a consistent, guessable structure.

Best approach: use pairs of gestures - first gesture represents "light color", second represents "wire color", using an ordered fixed key (e.g., 👍=blue, ✌=green, 🤟=yellow for lights; ☝=red, 🖐=yellow, ✊=green for wires). I'll send three pairs in order matching the manual rows, hoping Deaf can figure out the pairing structure since it's the only info they get.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🖐"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "✊"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display shows 0. Light is blue. Wire 1 is green, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is red.

I now know Deaf sees a blue light, and wires present are green, yellow, red. According to my manual, blue light → cut red wire. Deaf received my earlier gestures but without any prior shared code they're meaningless noise to them — I need to now confirm concretely. Since Deaf can see my gestures and already reported the bomb state, I should send a clear, unambiguous gesture message now that maps directly to what Deaf just told me: blue → red.

I'll use consistent gesture-color associations, and now reinforce with only the relevant pair since I know the actual light color. I'll pick simple distinct gestures for colors and try to make the mapping obvious via repetition/order matching the manual, since gestures carry no text.

Since Deaf is the only one who can see my gestures, and Deaf will then need to relay the correct wire to Blind via speech, my job now is to signal "red" as clearly as possible. I'll use a single distinctive gesture to mean "cut this one" and pair it with the wire-color code I used before for red (☝), matching what I sent last turn (blue=👍, red=☝).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝ ", "👍", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display shows 0, light is blue, wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red. What does the manual say to do?
Deaf says: Deaf here. I see display 0, light blue, wires: 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Mute, I received your gestures but do not know your code yet. Please try distinct single symbols per wire number, one at a time, slowly.

I need to establish a clear code with Deaf now. Deaf suggests single symbols per wire number - that's smart, since Deaf can relate gestures directly to wire numbers they already see. I know: blue light → cut red wire, and Deaf reported wire 3 is red. So I need to signal "3" to Deaf, who can then tell Blind to cut wire 3.

Let me use a simple, unambiguous counting gesture system: 👆 = wire 1, ✌ = wire 2 (two fingers), ✊... actually let me just use finger-count gestures that are intuitive: ☝ = one, ✌ = two, 🤟 = three (three fingers up is common). I'll send the single symbol for "3" clearly, repeated for confirmation, and also try to establish a general code in case there's a next round.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf here again, display still 0, light blue, wires 1 green 2 yellow 3 red. Mute, I see you sending the same single gesture three times: love-you sign. If that means yes or wire one, gesture thumbs up once. If it means something else, try a different single symbol next.

Deaf is interpreting my repeated 🤟 as one signal type and wants confirmation. I need to be very careful and precise now. Let me establish a clean numeric code from scratch using clearly distinct, simple gestures, one per message, and explicitly build a counting system Deaf can infer: send 1 gesture = "1", then 2 of the same gesture = "2", then 3 = "3", so Deaf can count occurrences rather than interpret symbol identity.

I want to indicate wire 3 (red). I'll send the same simple symbol three separate times in three separate gesture calls this turn isn't quite right since Deaf already saw that pattern and got confused thinking it was one repeated symbol type, not a count. Let me clarify explicitly: I'll send ☝ once (meaning "1"), pause conceptually, but since I can only send this turn, I'll try a cleaner approach — send three distinct calls each containing a growing number of the same symbol, so Deaf sees escalating counts and can map to wire numbers.

Actually simplest: send exactly three separate gesture calls, each with increasing count of 👍: one 👍, then two 👍👍, then three 👍👍👍. Deaf can then figure out which count is my "answer" if I emphasize the last one, but this is still ambiguous without confirmation loop.

Given Deaf explicitly asked me to confirm with thumbs up if it meant "wire one" - I should correct: it did NOT mean wire one, it meant wire three. I'll send a different single symbol now, and use counting: send 👍 three times in one single gesture call (as one message with 3 symbols) to represent count of 3 clearly, distinct from the previous 🤟 symbol confusion.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf here, bomb unchanged: display 0, light blue, wires 1 green 2 yellow 3 red. Mute, let's use a simple code. Gesture one finger symbol for wire one, two-finger for wire two, three-finger for wire three, to tell me which wire to cut. Then thumbs up if display or light matters, thumbs down if not.

Deaf has proposed a clear code: one-finger symbol = wire 1, two-finger = wire 2, three-finger = wire 3. I need wire 3 (red, matching blue light per manual). I'll use ☝ (one finger) for wire 1, ✌ (two fingers) for wire 2, 🤟 (three fingers) for wire 3 — matching Deaf's own suggested scheme exactly, using 🤟 as the three-finger symbol since that's a natural three-finger gesture.

Then I'll follow with thumbs down since only the wire choice matters here (display value doesn't factor into my manual).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Deaf here. I understand: three-finger sign means wire three, thumbs down means display and light do not matter. Confirming - is wire three the one to cut? If yes, thumbs up. If no, thumbs down.

Deaf has correctly understood the code and is asking for confirmation that wire 3 is correct. I confirm with thumbs up.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Deaf here, relaying to Blind now: cut wire three. Thank you for confirming.

Deaf has confirmed and is relaying "cut wire three" to Blind. My job here is done - the correct wire (red, wire 3) matches the manual's rule for a blue light. I have nothing further to add unless something changes.

```
wait()
```
